thread:
anne: Hey team — prod deploys started failing in CI around 09:14 UTC. Deploy job gets a 401 from our API gateway then a 403 when the deployer tries to impersonate the SA. Logs show 'audience mismatch' in the token. Anyone seen this pattern before?

jay: Can you paste the exact error log lines and the CI step that obtains the token?

anne: Sure — here's the failing snippet from the runner (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T09:14:23Z deployer[worker-5]: GET /v1/apps/deploy -> 401 Authorization failed: invalid_token (aud claim: "https://identity.example.com")
2026-03-17T09:14:24Z deployer[worker-5]: attempted impersonation of svc-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -> 403 iam.googleapis.com: permission denied: iamcredentials.generateAccessToken
```

infra-bot: Deploy job #4827 triggered by commit 9f3a2c — runner image: gha-runner-prod:v12. :robot_face:

sre_tony: Two quick things to check: audience (aud) in the JWT coming from the runner, and the IAM role on the service account. Sounds like the token audience is not what the API expects, and/or the CI principal lost iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (or equivalent) so impersonation fails.

support_terry: If you recently tightened least-privilege, we often see this when a role binding removed roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator or if the workload identity pool audience changed.

anne: We did a permission audit last night and removed some broad roles. The runner uses Workload Identity to exchange a federated token for the SA. How do I check the audience quickly?

jay: Run this locally from the runner host or replicate with gcloud/federated credentials. Example to print the ID token / aud:
```
# simulate the OIDC token exchange
gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences="https://identity.example.com" --impersonate-service-account=svc-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# or inspect the JWT header/payload
curl -s "https://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience=https://identity.example.com" -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" | jq -r .payload | base64 --decode
```
If aud doesn't match what the API checks, API will reject it.

anne: I tried printing the token — aud is "https://identity.example.com" which is what we expected, but the error persisted. The audit log shows the runner principal making an iamcredentials.generateAccessToken call and getting PERMISSION_DENIED.

sre_tony: That clarifies it — the runner principal can produce tokens but hasn't been granted the IAM permission to act on behalf of that specific SA. For impersonation you need the service account to grant the principal roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (or roles/iam.serviceAccountUser depending on flow). Example binding:
```
# grant token creator on the service account
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding svc-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/12345/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/pool/attribute.repository/gha-runner" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
```
Alternatively, temporarily add the project-level role to debug.

support_terry: Also confirm the IAM Conditions if you use them — a condition could block generateAccessToken for the specific audience or lifetime. Conditions often trip us when tightening perms.

anne: We do have an IAM condition restricting token lifetime to <= 1h and allowed audiences to a small set. The CI federation identity was recently updated to a new audience string in the pool config — I bet that's the mismatch.

jay: Steps to repro locally: 1) fetch token from oidc provider, 2) exchange with Workload Identity for SA token, 3) call the API. If step 2 fails with PERMISSION_DENIED then it's IAM binding; if step 3 fails with invalid aud then the pool/ API mismatch.

anne: Quick patch we applied: re-added roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator for the CI runner principal on svc-deploy, and adjusted the pool audience to include the older string. After that deploys retried and started succeeding. Monitoring shows no failures for 20m. :white_check_mark:

sre_tony: Nice. Follow-ups:
- Rotate the CI runner federated config to canonical audience and deploy a config change window.
- Replace broad project-level bind with the minimal principalSet binding to the specific SA.
- Add a pipeline test that does an end-to-end token exchange + API call on every release so we catch regressions early.

support_terry: I'll open a support ticket to track rolling back the last night permission changes with a runbook for regranting the exact role if we need to.

anne: Thanks all — saving the runbook notes here for the postmortem. Steps that fixed it: 1) add roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to svc-deploy for runner principal, 2) include older aud in pool while migrating, 3) run E2E smoke in CI. :memo: :eyes:

jay: Also consider monitoring IAM audit logs for PERMISSION_DENIED on iamcredentials.generateAccessToken — we can add an alert to channel #eng-oncall.

anne: Will do. Closing this thread as resolved for now — will follow up in the postmortem with exact policy diffs.
